title: QPI-DeepONet-MAC: A Scalable and Stable Hybrid Classical-Quantum Architecture for Physics-Informed Deep Operator Networks
authors: Said Lantigua, José Valencia, Gilson Giraldi, Renato Portugal, Jonas Maziero
abstract: General operator learning for parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) is a fundamental challenge at the intersection of artificial intelligence and physics-based modeling. Physics-informed Deep Operator Networks (PI-DeepONets) incorporate governing equations into learning, but face optimization difficulties in high dimensions. Quantum extensions offer additional representational capacity, yet their trainability can be hindered by barren plateaus. Here, we introduce QPI-DeepONet-MAC, a hybrid quantum-classical architecture that integrates parameterized quantum circuits into PI-DeepONets through a multiplicative-and-additive coupling (MAC) of classical representations and quantum expectation values. We prove analytically that the proposed architecture retains universal operator approximation capabilities. Furthermore, we derive bounds on quantum parameter gradients, establishing explicit conditions to avoid barren plateaus alongside a scaling criterion for trainability. Additionally, we derive a lower bound on the number of sensors required for a target accuracy, directly linking sampling requirements to input function regularity, domain dimension, and PDE dynamical growth. Finally, we propose an informational regularization scheme based on quantum coherence and state fidelity dynamics to prevent coherence loss and preserve quantum structure during training. Together, these results establish a theoretical foundation for quantum-enhanced physics-informed operator learning and position QPI-DeepONet-MAC as a scalable, stable framework for solving parametric PDEs.
summary: This paper introduces QPI-DeepONet-MAC, a novel hybrid architecture that merges classical DeepONets with parameterized quantum circuits to solve parametric PDEs. It tackles the limitations of standard PI-DeepONets by providing theoretical guarantees on stability, trainability (avoiding barren plateaus), and approximation accuracy. This establishes a robust, quantum-enhanced framework for physics-informed operator learning.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental challenge of general operator learning for parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) at the intersection of AI and physics-based modeling.
main_result: They propose QPI-DeepONet-MAC, a hybrid quantum-classical architecture, and provide theoretical guarantees including universal approximation capability, gradient bounds to avoid barren plateaus, and a lower bound on required sensor numbers.
method: The method combines Physics-Informed Deep Operator Networks (PI-DeepONets) with parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) via a multiplicative-and-additive coupling (MAC) mechanism.
model_or_system: The model is designed to approximate an operator G that maps a solution function u satisfying a set of physical PDEs. It integrates classical neural network components (DeepONet) with quantum expectation values derived from PQCs.
key_observables: The loss function minimizes physical constraints including initial conditions (LIC), boundary conditions (LBC), the PDE itself (LPDE), and source/solution terms (LSOL).
important_parameters: Quantum parameters (global tensor Xi_nu), classical weights (W_B, W_T), and regularization weights (lambda_COE, lambda_FID).
main_assumptions: The architecture retains universal operator approximation capabilities, and the stability is ensured by an informational regularization scheme based on quantum coherence and state fidelity.
figures_summary: Figure 1 and 2 show schematics of the unstacked and stacked PI-DeepONet architectures, respectively. Figure 3 details the unstacked QPI-DeepONet-MAC architecture, highlighting the MAC combination block.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon classical DeepONet structures by integrating quantum components. It details the mathematical formulation of the hybrid model, derives theoretical bounds on gradients and sampling requirements, and proposes a regularization scheme to maintain quantum structure during training.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it proposes a concrete, theoretically grounded framework for using quantum resources (PQCs) to enhance the solvability and stability of complex, high-dimensional PDEs, which is a major focus in quantum simulation and quantum machine learning for physics.
